actual_level_read: Cached primary abstract reread directly in full on 2026-10-18; no full-text verification claimed.
primary_quotes: Here we compare the biological effects of reading an electronic book on a light-emitting device (LE-eBook) with reading a printed book in the hours before bedtime.

Participants reading an LE-eBook took longer to fall asleep and had reduced evening sleepiness, reduced melatonin secretion, later timing of their circadian clock, and reduced next-morning alertness than when reading a printed book.
numerical_changes: 미확인 10분·25.7/15.8분·55%·1.5시간·22:31/21:01를 이득에서 삭제. 새로운 수치 없음. 한 시간 생활 권고는 검증된 threshold 아님을 유지.
scope_changes: Multiple pre-bedtime hours from abstract made explicit in easy/benefit; one-hour recommendation no longer asserted as measured threshold.
limitations: Full text unavailable. Exact exposure hours/repeated nights and participant denominator are not claimed in r2. Unverified numerical results removed; no numerical error is asserted.
Abstract supports hours before bedtime only; it does not establish the effect of one-hour exposure or a one-hour abstinence threshold.
No primary numerical conflict established and no formal correction notice identified in cached metadata (three Comment in items only).
Full-text attempts remained HTTP500/403 or recaptcha; successful HTTP200 did not supply article text. Raw responses and provenance remain beside proposal.
Original limitations regarding small controlled sample, ordinary phone brightness/duration and night mode remain inherited cautions; no new estimates or safety guarantee added.
approval_provenance: Independent reviewer authorized abstract-only r2 proposal, not publication approval. Frozen r1, strict entry and source untouched.
